## Overview

This week, we will cover the basics of the R language,
the Positron IDE,
and data structures and data types in R.
R is a great tool for
statistical analysis and visualization of any kind of data,
including omics data sets.
We will also start writing our R code in Quarto documents:
Markdown files with executable code chunks.

At the start of Monday's class, we'll install Positron and set up its connection to OSC
by following the [Positron setup page](./w12a_positron-setup.qmd).

There is only one class this week, on Monday,
because of Veteran's Day on Wednesday.
Instead of a Wednesday class, please work through the
[self-study section on R vectors and data types](./w12a_r-basics.qmd#self-study-vectors-and-data-types)
at the end of Monday's lecture page
before next week's classes, which will build on it.

## Lectures & Learning goals

Some of the things you will learn this week:

#### [Positron setup](./w12a_positron-setup.qmd)

-   Installing Positron and connecting it to OSC

#### [Introduction to R, Positron, and Quarto](./w12a_r-basics.qmd)

-   The Positron layout and the functions of its different regions and panes
-   The basics of interacting with R by using R as a calculator
-   Defining a variable/object in R, and assigning values/data to them
-   Calling R functions
-   Installing and loading R packages
-   Getting help in R
-   Writing, running, and rendering R code in a Quarto document
-   _Self-study:_ the vector data structure, R's main data types
    (`character`, `integer`, `double` and `logical`), and comparisons
